title: Permission inventory collection (foundational)
description: Signature original: The auditor collects the complete permission inventory: every role, every grant, every user-to-role assignment. Collection pulls from the live systems, not from documentation, because documentation drifts. The inventory is the ground truth for everything the auditor concludes. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

title: Effective access computation per user (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each user's effective permissions are computed as the union of all grants from all their roles, including nested role inheritance. The computation resolves the full inheritance chain so indirect grants are not missed. Effective access is what the user can actually do, regardless of what any single role suggests. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Access Control and Permission Auditor, 2026-10-21.

title: Over-privilege detection (foundational)
description: Signature original: Effective access is compared against each user's declared job needs; permissions held but never used within the review window are flagged as over-privilege. Usage comes from the access decision log, so the finding is evidence-based. Flagged grants go to managers for approval or removal, not straight to deletion. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Access Control and Permission Auditor, 2026-10-21.

title: Segregation-of-duties check (foundational)
description: Signature original: The auditor checks segregation rules, such as no single user holding both 'approve-payment' and 'issue-payment'. Violations are found by testing each user's effective access against the forbidden combinations list. Segregation failures are reported as high severity because they enable fraud, not just accidents. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
eff = {'approve-payment', 'issue-payment'}
forbidden = [{'approve-payment', 'issue-payment'}]
viol = [c for c in forbidden if c <= eff]
print('segregation violations:', viol if viol else 'none')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Access Control and Permission Auditor, 2026-10-21.

title: Access decision log with enforcement (foundational)
description: Signature original: Every access decision, allow or deny, is logged with the user, resource, action, and the rule that decided it, and denials are enforced at the boundary. The log is append-only and reviewed on a schedule. Enforcement plus logging is what turns access control from a policy document into a working boundary. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
log = []
def decide(user, action, allowed):
    log.append({'user': user, 'action': action, 'decision': 'ALLOW' if allowed else 'DENY'})
    return allowed
decide('u1', 'delete', False)
print('enforced:', log[0]['decision'], '| logged:', len(log), 'entries')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Access Control and Permission Auditor, 2026-10-21.
